attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same pair: the son of Cleitophon and Leucippe of Emesa, brought to the faith by the monk Onuphrius, and his wife Episteme, both beheaded under the governor Ursus. It prints an apolytikion and a kontakion that name them both, taken here; the Οἶκος and the Κάθισμα on the same page are not kinds the schema holds and are not drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.11.2025 (5. новембар ст. ст.) — „Преп. муч. Галактион и Епистима.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, and the heading is AN ENUMERATED PAIR — Галактион and Епистима — so section 5 counts two names, two folders are owed a row, and the corpus holds both. Quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Преп. муч.» is exactly the `venerable-martyr` both folders hold, and `monk` is the tonsure the body gives him. `dates` WIDENED from a flat «c. 250» to 250–253: saint.gr puts the pair in the third century under Decius, which is where the 250 came from, and this entry closes «пострадаше и венце на небу примише 253. год.» — they suffered and received their crowns in heaven in 253. Three years apart, two books, nothing chosen. **AND THE BOOK PUTS THEM IN A DIFFERENT CITY FROM THE ONE THEIR DISPLAY NAMES CARRY.** «Родом из града Едесе у Финикији» — from the city of EDESSA in Phoenicia, where the Russian calendar’s own name form is «Галактион Емесский (Финикийский)», EMESA in Phoenicia, and this corpus’s display name is «of Emesa». The province is the same in both and the city is not. NOTHING WAS RENAMED and no `locations` key was made; the disagreement is recorded here and in the life, which is `docs/CORPUS.md` section 3 on two sources disagreeing. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF A HOUSEHOLD. His mother Левкипија was BARREN UNTIL SHE WAS BAPTISED; she then brought her own husband to the true faith, and baptised and raised her son in it. When Galaction came of an age to marry, his good mother reposed and his father betrothed him to a maiden, Episteme. He would not enter marriage on any terms, and instead counselled her FIRST TO BE BAPTISED AND THEN TO BE TONSURED AT THE SAME HOUR AS HIMSELF. The two withdrew to Mount Публион, he to a men’s and she to a women’s monastery, and each proved a true luminary in his own: first at labour, first at prayer, first in humility and obedience, first in love. THEY NEVER LEFT THEIR MONASTERIES AND NEVER SAW ONE ANOTHER AGAIN UNTIL BEFORE DEATH. A bitter persecution came and both were brought to trial; and when Galaction was being mercilessly scourged, EPISTEME WEPT, AND THEN THEY SCOURGED HER TOO. Then they cut off their hands, then their feet, then at last their heads. NO `related` ROW ADDED AND THREE PEOPLE ARE NAMED. Episteme is `related` here in both directions already. The mother Левкипија is no folder this corpus holds. And «Евтолије», who took their bodies and buried them honourably, who had FIRST BEEN A SLAVE OF EPISTEME’S PARENTS AND AFTERWARDS A MONK TOGETHER WITH GALACTION, AND WHO WROTE THE LIFE OF THE TWO, is no folder either — and he is the book’s own source for the entry, which is worth recording even though nothing can be done with it. NO `locations`: Edessa, Phoenicia and Mount Publion are three places and this folder has never held the key. THE FOLD: `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured «Галактион» as held by `galaction-of-vologda`, so this form makes a TWO-member fold where the string had one holder and no key; the key is in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Galaction și Epistimia (a common of martyrs, printed for the two of them together; «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own spelling)

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength they overthrew the tormentors, and broke the powerless presumption of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Tὴν λαμπρὰν ξυνωρίδα τῶν μαρτύρων τιμήσωμεν ὥσπερ συζυγίαν ἀρίστην καὶ κλειτὴν καὶ θεόφρονα· τὸν θεῖον Γαλακτίωνα πιστοί, ὁμοῦ σὺν Ἐπιστήμῃ τῇ σεμνῇ. Δι' ἀσκήσεως γὰρ πόνων ἀθλητικὴν ἐξήνθησαν φαιδρότητα. Δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι δι' ὑμῶν πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Γαλακτίων και Επιστήμη», and it names them both.

english.text: Let us honour the bright pair of martyrs as a wedded couple most excellent, renowned and godly-minded: the divine Galaction, O faithful, together with the modest Episteme. For through the labours of ascetic struggle they brought to flower the radiance of the contest. Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Μαρτύρων Χριστοῦ, τοῖς δήμοις ἠριθμήθητε, ἀγῶσι στεῤῥοῖς, φαιδρῶς ἀγωνισάμενοι, Γαλακτίων ἔνδοξε, σῦν συζύγῳ σεπτῇ καὶ συνάθλῳ σου, Ἐπιστήμη, τῷ μόνῳ Θεῷ, πρεσβεύοντες ἄμφω ὑπὲρ πάντων ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Άγιοι Γαλακτίων και Επιστήμη», and it names them both.

english.text: You were numbered among the companies of the martyrs of Christ, having contended brightly in steadfast struggles — glorious Galaction, with your honoured wife and fellow-contender Episteme — both of you interceding with the only God for us all.

hymns.text: Мученицы Твои, Господи,/ во страданиих своих венцы прияша нетленныя от Тебе, Бога нашего,/ имуще бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложиша,/ сокрушиша и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Тех молитвами// спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь мучеников»

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from thee, our God; for having thy strength they cast down the tormentors and shattered the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: Мученик Христовых полком причтостеся,/ добре храбрствовавшим,/ светло подвизавшеся, Галактионе славне,/ с честною сопружницею и сострадавшею тебе Епистимиею,// Единому Богу непрестанно молитеся о всех нас.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак мучеников»

english.text: Ye were numbered with the regiments of Christ's martyrs, who warred well, and ye contended in splendour, O glorious Galaction, with thy honoured wife Episteme, who suffered together with thee: pray unceasingly to the one God for us all.

death.note: **Two books three years apart, and the interval holds both; it was a flat «c. 250» before this reading.** saint.gr: «Οι Άγιοι Γαλακτίων και Επιστήμη έζησαν τον 3ο αιώνα μ.Χ., όταν αυτοκράτορας ήταν ο Δέκιος» — the third century, under the emperor Decius, whose reign is where the 250 came from, the page printing no year of its own. The Охридски пролог for 5. новембар ст. ст. closes its entry «Он и написа житије ових дивних Христових мученика, који пострадаше и венце на небу примише 253. год.» — they suffered and received their crowns in heaven in 253, a year three past the end of Decius. Nothing is chosen and the basis stays traditional.
